items.stem: Complete the statement: In the absence of a partnership agreement, profits and losses are shared …
items.answer: equally

items.stem: State three provisions of the Partnership Act 1890 that apply when there is no agreement.
items.answer: Profits and losses shared equally; no interest on capital; no partners' salaries; no interest on drawings; 5% interest on partners' loans.

items.stem: Explain why partners should have a written partnership agreement.
items.answer: It avoids disputes by setting out capital, profit sharing, salaries, interest and drawings; otherwise the Act's rules apply, which may be unfair to a partner who works more or invests more.
items.markingKey: Avoids disputes/clear rules [1]; Act may be unfair [1] [2]

deducted from profit and credited to the partner

items.markingKey: added to profit in the appropriation account and debited to the partner's current account. It is a charge on the partner [1]

items.stem: Explain why a partner's salary is shown in the appropriation account and not as an expense.
items.answer: Partners are owners, not employees; their salary is a way of sharing profit to reward work, so it is an appropriation of profit.
items.markingKey: Partners are owners [1]; reward/share of profit [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain the purpose of charging interest on drawings.
items.answer: It discourages early or excessive withdrawals and compensates partners who leave money in the business.

items.stem: Explain why partners usually keep fixed capital accounts with separate current accounts.
items.answer: Capital accounts show the agreed long-term investment, which is the basis for interest on capital; all changes from profits and drawings go through current accounts.

items.stem: Explain what a debit balance on a partner's current account indicates and why it may be a concern.
items.answer: The partner has taken out more than their profit entitlement, so they owe the firm; persistent debit balances reduce the firm's capital and liquidity.

The agreement provides for interest on capital at 10% per annum and annual salaries: Priya $17,000. Profit for the year was $103,600. An accounts assistant deducted partners' salaries as an expense to find profit, then deducted them again in the appropriation account, giving residual profit of $61,800. State the mistake made and give the correct residual profit.
items.answer: Salaries are appropriations of profit only – they must be deducted once, in the appropriation account. Correct residual profit: $78,800.

Lina, Sipho and Ines are partners sharing profits and losses 3:2:1. Capitals are Lina $82,000, Sipho $67,000, Ines $58,000. The agreement provides for interest on capital at 4% per annum and annual salaries: Lina $18,000, Sipho $12,000. Interest on drawings has been calculated as Lina $840, Sipho $590, Ines $650. Profit for the year was $126,000. (a) Calculate the residual profit to be shared in the profit-sharing ratio. (b) Evaluate whether the profit-sharing arrangements of Volcano Spices are fair to all partners.
items.answer: (a) $89,800.00 (b) Interest on capital rewards investment, salaries reward work and the ratio shares the rest; fairness depends on each partner's capital, time and skills.

Samuel and Lina are partners sharing profits and losses 2:1. Capitals are Samuel $29,000, Lina $22,000. The agreement provides for interest on capital at 8% per annum and annual salaries: Samuel $6,000. Profit for the year was $143,400. A junior clerk calculated the closing balance on Samuel's current account as $132,000. Identify the error and state the correct balance.
items.answer: Drawings were credited (added) instead of debited. Correct balance: $70,200.
